requested_remedy: unlawful self-dealing and/or receipt of unauthorized profits in relation to 2 state-owned mining projects in Mongolia
parties: Plaintiff: Agency for Policy Coordination on State Property and Erdenet Mining Corporation and Erdene Oyu Tolgoi LLC

Defendant: Batbold Sukhbaatar and Cheong Choo Young and Kim Hak Seon and Catrison Limited and Genetrade Limited and Midlink International Limited and Lovitas Limited and Infinite Properties Limited and Ever Global Trading Limited and Captial World Development Limited and Gateview Development Limited and Klaford Services Limited

facts.F1: The proceedings were initiated in 2020 by the three Plaintiffs seeking injunctive relief under Section 21M of the High Court Ordinance.
facts.F2: The underlying proceedings were in Mongolia, alleging that the 1st Defendant had engaged in unlawful self-dealing and/or received unauthorized profits in relation to 2 state-owned mining projects.
facts.F3: Interlocutory relief in the form of an injunction order was granted in November 2020 and later amended on 4 December 2020.
facts.F4: On 18 November 2021, the underlying proceedings in Mongolia were dismissed with no appeal.
facts.F5: From late 2020 until 2022, correspondence was sent to the three Plaintiffs, and written confirmations were obtained that each of the Plaintiffs had not made any request for litigation to be brought against the Defendants.
facts.F6: The Defendants obtained written confirmations from the Prosecutor General and Deputy Prosecutor General of Mongolia, and the Mongolian Independent Authority Against Corruption, stating that King & Spalding did not have any authority to pursue legal proceedings.
facts.F7: Eventually, the various legal representatives ceased to act in the litigation worldwide.
facts.F8: In Hong Kong, Zhong Lun applied to cease to act for the Plaintiffs by summons dated 11 July 2022 and was granted an order on 1 September 2022.
facts.F9: On 30 August 2022, the Defendants applied by two summonses to discharge or strike out the present proceedings, served on Zhong Lun prior to the cease to act order and delivered to the Plaintiffs before the hearing on 13 October 2022.
facts.F10: At no point did the Plaintiffs indicate opposition, nor did they appear at the hearing.
facts.F11: Baigal Enkh-Amgalan provided expert evidence on the position under Mongolian law.
facts.F12: A related case in Singapore was not considered of significant assistance to the Hong Kong court.
facts.F13: The Plaintiffs failed to update the court about the dismissal of the Mongolian proceedings and did not disclose the authority issue at the outset.

facts.F10: The appellant leaned backwards against her, and she tried to straighten herself and in order to resist the appellant, she arched backwards.

facts.F12: She stepped back at him. An argument then ensued.

facts.F1: The plaintiff and the defendant entered into a Formal Agreement for Sale and Purchase on 21st March 1997 for the purchase of Flat A, 8th floor, Champion Building, Nos. 301-309 Nathan Road, Kowloon.
facts.F2: The plaintiff paid a deposit of $1,000,000 to the defendant.
facts.F3: The agreement was subject to a tenancy for two years from 1st November 1996 until 31st October 1998 for a portion of the property.
facts.F4: The defendant failed to provide the title deeds to the plaintiff's solicitors within the required time frame, and the defendant's solicitors did not supply the original or certified copy of the Crown Lease as required by the agreement and the Conveyancing and Property Ordinance.
facts.F5: The plaintiff's solicitors requested certified copies of the Crown Lease and other documents, which were not provided by the defendant's solicitors until 17th June 1997.

facts.F7: The defendant's solicitors failed to provide a completely legible copy of the Crown Lease, despite repeated requests.
facts.F8: The scheduled completion date was on or before 20th June 1997.
facts.F9: The defendant's solicitors had not shown good title by the time of the scheduled completion.
facts.F10: The conveyancing expenses and agent's commission were in the sums of $78,250 and $50,000 respectively.
